citations.text: National Rivers and Streams Assessment 2018-19 Technical Support Document
USDA Forest Service 2011, Watershed Condition Classification Technical Guide (FS-978)

limitations: Road density does not count actual outfalls or establish whether runoff is treated.
The 1 km/km² breakpoint is a screening judgment.

USFS watershed-condition guidance classes road density more strictly (good under 1, impaired over 2.4 miles per square mile, about 0.62 and 1.49 km/km²), derived from salmonid watersheds. EASI keeps the NRSA-anchored national screen and discloses the stricter alternative.

metrics.howToMeasure: Base-flow index (% of streamflow from baseflow); a higher baseflow share indicates a more stable, groundwater-supported flow regime. metrics.sourceCitation: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 13), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.14-provisional
metrics.howToMeasure: Mean bank angle; very steep banks indicate incision and very flat banks an over-widened, aggrading channel, so departure from the reference core in either direction departs from reference. Direction resolved at the Northeastern Highlands review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21), consistent with the width-to-depth and bankfull-height treatment. low_tail flat added at the adversarial review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21): a regraded or naturally gentle bank holds at the Functioning edge instead of being penalized, because the flat tail is not symmetric evidence of degradation and the framework's stated use is restoration evaluation.
metrics.methodContext: At the left and the right bank of each transect, lay a pole about one meter long against the bank and read its angle from horizontal with a clinometer, in degrees. The value is the mean of the 22 readings.

metrics.howToMeasure: Log relative bed stability; departure from the reference core in EITHER direction departs from reference (negative excess fines, positive an armored, sediment-starved bed, the classic below-impoundment failure). The pilot's rising direction scored armored beds 1.0 and left Sediment continuity blind to its textbook failure mode. Two-sided form is an owner decision at the adversarial review gate, 2026-08-21.
metrics.methodContext: Computed, not read in the field. It is the base 10 logarithm of the ratio of the geometric mean particle diameter to the largest diameter the bankfull flow can move, from the particle count, reach slope, bankfull depth, wood tally and residual pools, with the NRSA physical habitat calculations.

curve.layerName: USEPA NRSA 2013-24 (L3 ecoregion 13), StreamCurves regional analysis, methodology 0.14-provisional

curveCaveats: The reference pool's lower quartile for this metric is zero: at least a quarter of the pool has a value of zero, so the curve has no fitted lower anchor. It rises in a straight line from 0 at zero to 1 at 3, the pool's upper quartile. Read the band as a coarse sort, not a measurement.

The reference stations for this curve were borrowed from NARS-9 region ecoregion XER because this ecoregion has too few least-disturbed stations of its own. 66 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from NARS-9 region XER, 18 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on drainage area, channel slope, air temperature. Every station drains to this ecoregion's faunal province. The national scale analysis supports this metric at Level II, finer than the level borrowed from, so the transfer risk is moderate and the expectation may not represent local conditions.

In the discrimination check this curve scored pressured stations above reference stations (area under the curve 0.38), so the score may not track condition here. Read it with the other metrics of the function.

criteriaSource.title: Nearby dam-proximity proxy

citations.text: USACE National Inventory of Dams

limitations: A mapped dam count is a proximity screen and cannot confirm passability or the severity of a barrier.
NID carries about 91,000 regulated dams while the National Aquatic Barrier Inventory maps over 500,000 barriers of all sizes, so zero mapped dams is frequently a false negative for passage.
Query failure is unscored, not Good.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 24 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 1 curve is fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 2 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 1 carries the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The NARS-9 pool (XER): In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The Level II pool (10.1): In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. The Level I pool (10): In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough and the source promoted sites systematically. No other basis supports it either.
